newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu's Puerto Rico model a dream, Egypt says.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu's Puerto Rico model a dream, Egypt says.

text.p: A senior Egyptian official said on Saturday Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was dreaming if he thought Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza could be limited to a Puerto Rican-style autonomy.
Osama el-Baz, political adviser to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, said Netanyahu must accept full Palestinian independence or risk sparking another intifada (uprising).
"The concept of establishing a Puerto Rico type of a state is ridiculous," Baz told a seminar in Amman. "I don't know if it is serious. He could be daydreaming."

He was responding to an Israeli report on Friday which said Netanyahu backed a Palestinian self-rule entity along the lines of Puerto Rico, an autonomous commonwealth in association with the United States, or Andorra, the tiny mountain principality between France and Spain famous for its ski resorts.
"The Palestinians are different," Baz said. "The Puerto Ricans never owned America."

He predicted the Israeli leader, elected in May on a platform which opposed the establishment of a Palestinian state or the trading of captured Arab land for peace, would have to make concessions in the face of public opposition both in Israel and the outside world.
"Between now and the spring you will see Prime Minister Netanyahu confronting seriously the matter of the future of the Palestinian territories," Baz said.

"He may not introduce 180 degree (change). He cannot abandon the hardline aspect of his ideas, but he will be compelled willy-nilly to introduce more balance between ideology and pragmatism," he added.

Baz said that if Netanyahu maintained his opposition to Palestinian statehood, the Palestinians "would not take this lying down. It would be their legitimate right to oppose it by whatever means available."
Baz said he hoped President Bill Clinton, re-elected to a second term on Tuesday, would re-affirm U.S. support for a full implementation of the Israeli-Palestinian accord on self-rule.

Netanyahu's government is locked in talks with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron signed by the previous government.

Arabs have urged immediate implementation of the Hebron deal followed swiftly by other agreed steps, including the release of more Palestinian prisoners from Israeli jails, free passage for Palestinians between self-rule areas, and further Israeli redeployment in the West Bank.

"What we are seeking is not raw, crude (U.S.) pressure on Israel," Baz said. "What is needed is a reaffirmation of the American position on issues like (Jewish) settlements, like the final status, like the necessity to implement in good faith agreements which have been previously signed."
